source_expressions.sketch_quote: Write R(z,A) = (z I - A)^{-1}. For spectral parameters lam, mu off the spectrum, the expanded identity is R(lam,A) - R(mu,A) = (mu - lam) R(lam,A) R(mu,A). For two operators and a common z off both spectra, R(z,A) - R(z,B) = R(z,A) (B-A) R(z,B). The first difference quotient in the spectral parameter is (R(lam,A)-R(mu,A))/(lam-mu) = - R(lam,A) R(mu,A); when lam=mu the same object is the derivative -R(lam,A)^2.
source_displays: Glück Prop. 2.2.9: R(λ,a) − R(μ,a) = (μ − λ) R(λ,a) R(μ,a) for all λ, μ ∈ ρ(a).
Glück Ex. 2.3.2: ρ(a) → A, λ ↦ R(λ,a) is holomorphic and R'(λ,a) = −R(λ,a)^2.
Müger Ex. 13.29 (opposite convention R_a(λ)=(a−λ1)^{-1}): R_a(s)−R_a(t)=(s−t)R_a(s)R_a(t) for s,t ∈ F\σ(a); R_a(s)−R_b(s)=R_a(s)(b−a)R_b(s) for s ∈ F\(σ(a)∪σ(b)).

source_catalog_needs.proposer_text: R(λ,A) − R(μ,A) = (μ − λ) R(λ,A) R(μ,A), with R(z,A) = (z I − A)^{-1} and λ, μ off the spectrum of A.
On the same set, the z-derivative of R(·,A) at λ is −R(λ,A)^2.
R(z,A) − R(z,B) = R(z,A)(B − A)R(z,B) for z off both spectra. Same R convention as MPR0001.

hidden_target_representation.nodes: spectral parameters (λ, μ); repeated node λ=μ from holomorphy on ρ(A)
hidden_target_representation.claim: One first Newton DD of F in the spectral parameter: F[λ,μ] = −R(λ,A)R(μ,A), with F[λ,λ] = R'(λ,A) = −R(λ,A)^2. The two-operator identity is the same difference-quotient structure in the operator argument at fixed z, not a second F.

expected_proof_obligations: EQUALITY: R(λ,A)−R(μ,A)=(μ−λ)R(λ,A)R(μ,A) for λ,μ ∈ ρ(A) (Higham/Glück convention).
NEWTON_DD: (R(λ,A)−R(μ,A))/(λ−μ) = −R(λ,A)R(μ,A) = F[λ,μ] for λ≠μ in ρ(A).
DERIVATIVE / LIMIT / CONFLUENCE: μ→λ inside ρ(A) yields R'(λ,A)=−R(λ,A)^2 = F[λ,λ].
HYPOTHESES: λ,μ ∈ ρ(A); z ∈ ρ(A)∩ρ(B); do not require a disk around the spectrum; do not mix Müger's (A−zI)^{-1} sign into the Higham/Glück displays.

verifier_route.detail: B0 already implements the scalar instance (1/(λ−a)−1/(μ−a))/(λ−μ) + 1/((λ−a)(μ−a)) at (λ,μ,a)=(3,2,0) and reports ZERO. Finite-n matrix check: multiply the first identity on the left by (λI−A) and on the right by (μI−A). Hypotheses checker: λ,μ not in spec(A). Confluent clause is the declared holomorphic derivative, not a 0/0 the verifier must take.

source_expressions.sketch_quote: Let X = Z D Z^{-1} with D = diag(l_1,...,l_n). The directional derivative of f at X in direction E expands, in the eigenbasis, as a piecewise array: (Z^{-1} L_f(X,E) Z)_{ij} equals ((f(l_i)-f(l_j))/(l_i-l_j)) * (Z^{-1} E Z)_{ij} when l_i != l_j, and equals f'(l_i) * (Z^{-1} E Z)_{ii} when l_i = l_j. The same array is a single Hadamard product against the kernel of first difference quotients of f on the spectrum, including the repeated-eigenvalue diagonal.
source_displays: Noferini Thm 2.10 (C^1 restatement): L_f(A,E) = Z (F ∘ (Z^{-1} E Z)) Z^{-1} with F_ij = (f(D_ii)−f(D_jj))/(D_ii−D_jj) if D_ii ≠ D_jj and F_ij = f'(D_ii) otherwise.
Higham before Thm 3.9: f[l,m] = (f(l)−f(m))/(l−m) if l ≠ m, f[l,l] = f'(l).
Higham Thm 3.11 / Cor. 3.12: same kernel for diagonal / diagonalizable X with f ∈ C^{2n−1}(D), spec(X) ⊂ D.

source_catalog_needs.proposer_text: X = Z D Z^{-1}, D = diag(l_1,...,l_n), Z invertible. Off-diagonal: (Z^{-1} L_f(X,E) Z)_{ij} = ((f(l_i)−f(l_j))/(l_i−l_j)) (Z^{-1} E Z)_{ij} when l_i ≠ l_j.

On the equal-eigenvalue diagonal: (Z^{-1} L_f(X,E) Z)_{ii} = f'(l_i) (Z^{-1} E Z)_{ii} when l_i = l_j. Same L_f, Z, D as MPD0001. f is 2n−1 times continuously differentiable on an open set containing the l_i.

hidden_target_representation.claim: L_f(X,E) = Z ((f[l_i,l_j]) ∘ (Z^{-1} E Z)) Z^{-1}. Generic quotients and equal-eigenvalue derivatives are one first-DD / Loewner kernel, not two Piecewise programs. Diagonal confluence is Hermite order 1.

expected_proof_obligations: EQUALITY (off-diagonal): (Z^{-1} L_f(X,E) Z)_{ij} = f[l_i,l_j] (Z^{-1} E Z)_{ij} for l_i ≠ l_j.
HERMITE_DD / NEWTON_DD (diagonal): f[l,l] = f'(l) supplied by C^{2n−1}, not a verifier 0/0.
MASTER_INSTANCE / HADAMARD: L_f(X,E) = Z (K ∘ (Z^{-1} E Z)) Z^{-1} with K_ij = f[l_i,l_j].
HYPOTHESES: X diagonalizable, Z invertible, spec(X) ⊂ D open in ℝ or ℂ, f ∈ C^{2n−1}(D).
FORBIDDEN: do not require holomorphy; do not require X Hermitian; do not discharge Higham C^{2n−1} from Noferini C^1.

verifier_route.detail: No B0 smoke. Check Fréchet definition f(X+E)=f(X)+L_f(X,E)+o(||E||) against the Hadamard kernel on a small diagonalizable example (distinct eigenvalues, then a repeated pair). Scalar Loewner kernel (f(a)−f(b))/(a−b) vs f' is sympy. Do not residual the piecewise display against the DD definition — that is tautological. Hypotheses checker: C^{2n−1}, spec in D, Z invertible.

source_expressions.sketch_quote: Let A in C^{n x n} have distinct eigenvalues l_1..l_s with indices n_i (size of the largest Jordan block for l_i). The expanded form of f(A) changes with the Jordan data: if all n_i=1 and s=2, f(A) = f(l_1)*(A-l_2 I)/(l_1-l_2) + f(l_2)*(A-l_1 I)/(l_2-l_1); if a single Jordan block J_k(l) of size m, the strictly upper diagonals of f(J_k) are f^{(j)}(l)/j! for j=1..m-1. The scientific target is one polynomial p of degree < sum_i n_i with p^{(j)}(l_i)=f^{(j)}(l_i) for j=0..n_i-1 and f(A)=p(A), valid on both the distinct-eigenvalue and repeated-node strata.
source_displays: Higham–Lin 2013 Def. 3.2: f defined on the spectrum of A ∈ C^{n×n}; f(A):=p(A) where p is the unique polynomial of degree less than ∑ n_i satisfying p^{(j)}(λ_i)=f^{(j)}(λ_i), j=0:n_i−1, i=1:s.
Higham–Lin 2013 (3.4) / Def. 3.1: f(J_k) has f^{(j)}(λ_k)/j! on the j-th superdiagonal.
Higham–Lin 2013 square-root example (not a general branch rule): for f(t)=t^{1/2} principal, A=[[2,2],[1,3]], λ={1,4}, p(t)=(t+2)/3, A^{1/2}=p(A).

source_catalog_needs.proposer_text: If A has two distinct eigenvalues l_1, l_2 and all Jordan indices 1, the expanded formula is f(A) = f(l_1)(A−l_2 I)/(l_1−l_2) + f(l_2)(A−l_1 I)/(l_2−l_1).
If A is a single Jordan block J_m(l), the main diagonal of f(J_m) is f(l) and the j-th strict superdiagonal is f^{(j)}(l)/j! for j=1..m−1. The values f^{(j)}(l) are assumed to exist.

hidden_target_representation.claim: f(A):=p(A) for the unique osculatory interpolant p of those jets. Distinct-eigenvalue Lagrange and repeated-node Jordan Taylor blocks are one interpolant, not two Piecewise programs. Equivalent to the Jordan definition without holomorphy (Higham Thm 1.12).

expected_proof_obligations: EQUALITY: Lagrange two-pole formula when s=2 and n_i=1 (MPH0001).
HERMITE_DD: f(J_m(λ)) superdiagonal j equals f^{(j)}(λ)/j! (MPH0002).
BASIS_RECONSTRUCTION: f(A)=p(A) for the unique p of degree < ∑ n_i matching p^{(j)}(λ_i)=f^{(j)}(λ_i).
HYPOTHESES: jets exist through the Jordan index; A ∈ C^{n×n}; primary branch at every occurrence of an eigenvalue.
FORBIDDEN: do not insert holomorphy (that is Cauchy Def. 1.11); do not insert A Hermitian or A diagonalizable; do not attach Re t^{1/2}≥0 unless the instance is Higham's square-root example.

verifier_route.detail: No B0 smoke. 2×2 diagonalizable check of MPH0001; 2×2 Jordan block check of MPH0002. Hypotheses: jet existence, not holomorphy. Uniqueness of p is DERIVED from the definition, not an extra axiom. Scalar interpolant matching is sympy; the representation claim is f(A)=p(A) across both strata.

source_expressions.sketch_quote: f(A) is defined as (1/(2 π i)) * contour_integral_Gamma f(z) (z I - A)^{-1} dz, with Gamma a closed contour about the eigenvalues. Expanding the resolvent in a Jordan or eigenbasis recovers the usual block formulae; the same contour with denominator (z-t_1)...(z-t_k) produces the Newton coefficients of f. The compact object is the contour integral, not the expanded residue table.
source_displays: Higham–Lin 2013 Def. 3.3: f(A) = (1/(2πi)) ∮_Γ f(z)(zI−A)^{-1} dz, f analytic on and inside a closed contour Γ that encloses λ(A).
Higham–Lin 2013 §3.1.4: Defs 3.1, 3.2, 3.3 equivalent modulo analyticity for the Cauchy definition [Higham 2008 Thm 1.12].
de Boor (51), sibling only: Δ(t_{1:j}) f = (1/(2πi)) ∮ f(ζ)/w_{j,t}(ζ) dζ, under f entire in a disk of radius ρ, contour radius ρ'<ρ, nodes not in the annulus.
